## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Normalize keys on write so mixed-case entries can be retrieved, and expire entries when they reach their deadline.

## Changes

The pull request adds `Cache.set` and raises the default TTL from 60 to 300 seconds. It adds tests for round-trip lookup, the default TTL constant, and expiry with a custom TTL.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Normalize keys before storing them — After `set("ALPHA", 1)`, both `get("ALPHA")` and `get("alpha")` return `None`. `set` stores `"ALPHA"` as written, while `get` looks up `"alpha"`. — Callers that write mixed-case keys get cache misses immediately after a successful write. — Fix: Store the entry under `key.lower()` and extend `test_set_then_get_round_trip` with a mixed-case write.
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Expire entries at their deadline — With `ttl=1`, a read exactly one second after `set("alpha", 1)` still returns `1`. The new `set` records the deadline, and `get` removes the entry only when `expires < time.monotonic()`. — A caller reading at the deadline can treat stale data as a cache hit. — Fix: Use `expires <= time.monotonic()` at `app/cache.py:21` and extend `test_entries_expire`.

## Suggestions

- app/cache.py:7 — comments — Identify 300 seconds as the default TTL — An entry written with `Cache(ttl=1)` expires after one second, contrary to “Entries expire 300 seconds after they are written.” The write computes its deadline with `time.monotonic() + self._ttl`. — The comment gives maintainers the wrong retention period when a caller supplies a custom TTL.
- tests/test_cache.py:18 — tests — Test the default lifetime through the cache API — If `Cache()` reverted to a 60-second lifetime while `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL` remained 300, `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` would still pass because it checks only the constant. — A regression in the lifetime callers get from `Cache()` would pass the test intended to protect it. — Fix: Use the controlled clock from `test_entries_expire` to exercise the default lifetime through `set` and `get`.
